# Lotería de los Pueblos

URL: https://app.loteria.to
Languages of the game: Nahuatl (nah), Yucatec Maya (yua), Quechua Cusco-Collao (quz), Spanish (es), English (en). App interface: Spanish and English.
Price: free. Accounts: none. Ads: none. Use: non-commercial.

## What the game is

Lotería de los Pueblos is a progressive web app (installable, works offline after the first visit) that plays the traditional picture lotería, the Mexican bingo-like game of illustrated cards, with the cards called aloud in five languages instead of one. The deck has 54 original illustrations inspired by the nature, crafts and places of Mesoamerica and the Andes. Cards never show people. Every card has a name in each of the five languages.

## How a round works

1. One person creates a room (the cantor's screen) and shows its code and QR. Players join from their phones with the code, the link or the QR, choosing a name and a picture. A round needs at least 2 players; a room holds up to 20.
2. Each player gets one board (cartón) of 4 columns by 4 rows: 16 different cards drawn from the deck, at most 5 from the same group. Boards in the same room differ from each other. The board shows pictures only; a square's written name appears once that card has been called.
3. The cantor is an automatic voice. It calls each card once, in random order, one at a time, every 6 to 20 seconds as the organiser set. Every player sees the picture and hears the name in their own spoken language at the same moment.
4. Each player gets three written spellings of the card in their spoken language and picks the right one. The first correct pick earns 2 points, other correct picks earn 1, and a wrong pick earns 0 with a friendly "¡Casi!" and one more try. Points only break ties within the round.
5. Everyone who has the called card on their board crosses it off with a bean, whether they picked correctly or not.
6. The first player to cross off all 16 squares calls "¡Lotería!". If several complete on the same card, the one with the most points wins; equal points share. Then "Otra ronda" starts a new round with new boards.

Each player chooses two languages independently: the app language (Spanish or English) and the spoken language (any of the five). A Spanish speaker can keep the app in Spanish and hear Nahuatl to practise it. A "listen" mode calls only the word, to learn by ear.

## Other ways to play

- Solo mode: play offline against 1 to 3 computer players at easy, normal or hard level.
- Paper mode: print PDF boards and play with beans, no phones. One screen can call for a whole classroom.

## Who it is for

Multilingual families (grandparents call in their language while children look for pictures), classrooms and community centres, and people learning a heritage language. Designed to include everyone: adjustable text size, high contrast, keyboard support, no accounts, and your name and marks stay on your device.

## Audio, content and licences

The card names are voiced with synthetic voices generated with Meta MMS-TTS, licensed CC BY-NC 4.0, which is why the game is non-commercial. Words in Indigenous languages are only called once reviewed by native speakers; review status is tracked per word. See https://app.loteria.to/creditos for art, typefaces (Atkinson Hyperlegible, Bricolage Grotesque, Noto Sans under the SIL Open Font License) and software credits.
